analysis.title: In Credit: Tech it to the limit (2 November 2026)
key_insights: CCC spreads in US high yield widened to about 1,100bps over US Treasuries. The quality gap is at historic extremes, with BB-CCC around 1,260bps and B-CCC around 1,140bps, which the author reads as the early-to-mid stage of a credit stress cycle.

Weakness in CCCs and distressed names, plus sharp single-name moves, stalled HY primary issuance. CCCs are only about 6% of the HY index, and the broader BB and B universe still looks fundamentally sound.
The key question is whether stress stays at the bottom of HY or migrates up. The report says to watch BB and B spreads for a signal that CCC weakness is spilling into a broader HY event.

Core government curves steepened last week in the US, Germany and the UK. The US 2-year yield fell about 9bps and the 30-year fell about 1bp, on safe-haven demand (French politics, AI concerns) and a partial repricing of near-term growth risk.
The Fed held at 3.75%-4%. Chair Kevin Warsh framed the hold as needing to 'accumulate more information'. The probability of a December hike fell from about 90% to about 70%.

The ECB held at 2.5% and rejected a hike, citing no evidence that higher energy prices were feeding second-round effects on wages and prices. The BoJ held at 1.25% with a hawkish message, and markets expect a December hike.

AI capex doubts gave a continuing asset-allocation bid to high-quality government bonds. Brent finished the week at $118 and the bond market impact was muted because investors saw the disruption as temporary.

The UK budget on 28 October produced the first sustained gilt rally since the start of summer. The 30-year gilt fell 18bps to 5.714%, driven by lower fiscal and term premium rather than lower inflation expectations. Markets price a near-certain BoE hike to 4% on 5 November.

The DMO cut planned issuance of gilts with 15+ year maturities to under 7% of total FY2026-27 supply (£250.6 billion total), the lowest share since 1990/91. Together with the BoE's QT overhaul, this may raise the relative attractiveness of swaps alongside physical gilts for long liability hedges.

IG credit was mixed. Global IG widened 1bp to 96bps, US IG widened 2bps to 93bps, Sterling IG was flat at 96bps and Euro IG tightened 4bps to 103bps. iTraxx Main tightened about 2bps to 66bps and CDX IG tightened 1bp to 62bps, both materially wider mid-week.

Alphabet and Amazon missed in Q3 2026 and reversed the week's risk-on tone. Alphabet's capex more than doubled y/y and search slowed. Amazon's trailing-12-month FCF was -$42.4 billion versus +$14.8 billion a year earlier. S&P revised Meta's outlook to negative. Oracle's bonds rallied after it committed to $10 billion of gross debt growth through FY2030.
Fitch put France on negative watch. A downgrade would mechanically pressure French bank ratings through sovereign-linked methodologies. The French spread over Bunds finished the week at about 164bps.

US HY spreads finished the week 6bps wider. CCCs widened 108bps in October and 380bps year-to-date versus 23bps for BBs and 43bps for single-Bs (JPMorgan). Q3 HY earnings are softer than the prior quarter, with weakness in consumer gaming, travel-sensitive credits and healthcare. The ICE BofA US HY CP Constrained Index returned -0.38%.

US HY retail funds took in $1.3 billion, the largest inflow in 12 weeks. Leveraged loan spreads are 18bps inside last week's 18-month high of 519bps, and the S&P UBS Leveraged Loan Index average price rose $0.21 to $93.56. Loan funds had their first weekly outflow in 18 weeks.

European HY returned about -1.2% in October (EUR hedged), the third-worst month of the year. CCCs returned -7%. Spreads widened 60bps month-to-date to 376bps and yields rose 43bps to 7.15%. Recordati priced a €4.5 billion-equivalent LBO financing, the largest European HY deal of 2026, and was downgraded to BB-/B1.

European LME news: Intrum agreed in principle a debt restructuring including a debt-for-equity swap. Grupo Antolin bondholders reportedly recovered 25%, pari passu with bank debt. Telecom Italia was upgraded to IG.

The Bloomberg US MBS Index returned +75bps for the week. Non-agency spreads widened 10bps in CRT M1 and non-QM A1, and 20bps in BBB non-QM M1s. Data centre SASB deals widened 5bps-40bps and data centre ABS widened 10bps.

EM debt returned sovereigns +0.58%, corporates +0.22% and local +0.11% in October. Oil hit $118 on Friday and fell to $106 at Monday's open on peace-talk prospects between Iran and Qatari mediators. Argentina reached an IMF staff-level agreement unlocking US$900 million, and Egypt hiked rates 100bps to 20%/21%.

market_movers.rationale: Alphabet's Q3 2026 results missed on revenue and EPS as capex more than doubled y/y. A slowdown in search raised concern that AI is cannibalising core advertising.
Amazon missed. Trailing-12-month free cash flow was -$42.4 billion versus +$14.8 billion a year earlier.
S&P revised Meta's outlook to negative on uncertainty over capex guidance and free operating cash flow.
Oracle committed to just $10 billion of gross debt growth through FY2030 and guided to $30 billion of FCF in FY29. Its bonds rallied.
Stellantis bonds widened early in the week on turnaround uncertainty, then reversed sharply after a Q3 2026 earnings beat.

sector_views.rationale: CCC spreads are at about 1,100bps with record dispersion versus BB and B. The report reads this as early-to-mid stage credit stress.
BB and B credits still look fundamentally sound, but their spreads are the signal to watch for spillover from CCCs.
Lower long-end gilt supply and the QT overhaul change supply dynamics. With CPI at 3.5% and breakevens at 3.33%, the report says a review of inflation hedge ratios remains compelling.

earnings_insights: Alphabet Q3 2026 (reported the week of 26 October): missed on revenue and EPS (basis not specified in the report). Capex more than doubled y/y and search slowed.
Amazon (reported): missed. Trailing-12-month FCF was -$42.4 billion versus +$14.8 billion a year earlier.
Oracle: management guided to $30 billion of FCF in FY29 (guidance) and committed to $10 billion of gross debt growth through FY2030.
Stellantis Q3 2026 (reported): earnings beat (figures not given).

US HY earnings: about a third of companies have reported. Results are softer than the previous quarter, which was the strongest quarter of HY earnings growth in four years. Weakness is in consumer gaming, travel-sensitive credits and healthcare.

macro_indicators.interpretation: The Fed held. Markets lean toward a less persistent hiking cycle.

macro_indicators.indicator: Probability of a December Fed hike
macro_indicators.interpretation: Market-implied odds fell after the front-end Treasury rally.
The ECB held and rejected a hike. Markets pared back expected tightening over the next 12 months.
The BoJ held with a hawkish message. Markets expect a December hike.
A fourth consecutive monthly increase. Breakeven inflation still fell, so the gilt rally reflected fiscal and term premium compression.
Markets price a near-certain hike to 4%.
Fell 18bps, with the sharpest move on and after the 28 October budget.
Still well above target, which supports reviewing inflation hedge ratios.

macro_indicators.reading: $118 a barrel at the week's close, $106 at Monday's open
macro_indicators.interpretation: The fall came as prospects for peace talks improved. Bond markets treated the disruption as temporary.
Political volatility and weak debt dynamics produced a safe-haven bid for Bunds.

macro_indicators.indicator: US house prices (FHFA HPI and S&P Cotality 20-City)

macro_indicators.interpretation: Builder incentives did not offset higher mortgage rates.

trade_ideas.description: Use swaps alongside physical gilts to implement longer UK liability hedges
trade_ideas.rationale: The DMO cut 15+ year gilt issuance to under 7% of supply and the BoE overhauled QT, which may make swaps relatively more attractive.

trade_ideas.description: Review inflation hedge ratios for UK DB pension schemes
trade_ideas.rationale: CPI is at 3.5% and breakevens at 3.33%, still well above target.

risk_factors: Stress in CCC credits migrating up to BB and B spreads and becoming a broader HY event.
AI capex financing wave and doubts about commercial returns on AI spending.
A French sovereign downgrade pressuring French bank ratings and European financials.
Higher energy prices and Middle East escalation, including possible escalation after the US midterms.
Higher mortgage rates slowing housing activity and prepayment speeds.
Weakness in consumer gaming, travel-sensitive credits and healthcare in HY earnings.
charts_described: Chart of the Week plots US high yield spread by rating bucket (CCC, B, BB) versus US Treasuries from Jan 2024 to Oct 2026, with a labeled reading of about 1,116bps on 30-Oct-26 and a y-axis from 0 to 1,200bps.
vol_and_positioning: CCC spreads of about 1,100bps with BB-CCC around 1,260bps and B-CCC around 1,140bps show record quality dispersion in US HY.
US HY retail funds took in $1.3 billion, the largest inflow in 12 weeks. Loan funds had their first weekly outflow in 18 weeks.
European HY: ETF demand gave a technical floor while managed accounts reduced exposure. The last week had a net outflow of €118 million, driven entirely by managed account redemptions.
iTraxx Main and CDX IG were materially wider mid-week before recovering to 66bps and 62bps.
There were no changes to global rates mandates last week.
geopolitical: Renewed escalation in the Middle East, with the Houthis continuing to attack Saudi Arabia.

Talks between Iran and Qatari mediators in Doha on a potential agreement to end the conflict. Iran's foreign minister Abbas Araghchi said the Strait of Hormuz could reopen within two days of an agreement.
Concern about possible escalation following the US midterms pushed oil to $118 before it fell to $106.
Israel's election produced no parliamentary majority. Neither Netanyahu's bloc nor Eisenkot's opposition reached 61 seats, and Arab parties are projected at 19 seats.
French political volatility and deteriorating debt dynamics. Fitch placed France on negative watch.

tension_points.bull_case: CCCs are only about 6% of the HY index, and the broader BB and B universe looks fundamentally sound. Retail HY funds saw the largest inflow in 12 weeks and some October concerns, including AI financing, have started to ease.
tension_points.bear_case: The BB-CCC gap at about 1,260bps looks like the early-to-mid stage of a credit stress cycle. CCCs widened 380bps year-to-date, primary issuance stalled, and Q3 HY earnings are softer.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A widening in BB and B spreads, which the report says to watch as the signal that CCC weakness is spilling into a broader HY event.

tension_points.bull_case: Oracle committed to limited gross debt growth of $10 billion through FY2030 and guided to $30 billion of FCF in FY29, and its bonds rallied.
tension_points.bear_case: Alphabet's capex more than doubled y/y with a search slowdown, Amazon's trailing FCF is -$42.4 billion, and S&P moved Meta's outlook to negative.

theme_stances.key_argument: Bifurcation between CCCs and higher-rated HY looks more like the early-to-mid stage of a credit stress cycle than its end.
